artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan correcting five empty-vector lake-build-guard.sh full-build invocations across four lean-extension source files, with a fake-lake runtime proof, exhaustive source-store audit, consumer-propagation record, and a usage-banner handoff.

user_decision.question: The dispatch's acceptance clause asks to deploy the affected extension and confirm the regenerated .claude/** copies carry the fix, but the `lean` extension is not active in this repository (.claude-extensions.json lists core, email, literature, memory, nix, nvim), so no lean artifact is regenerated here. Should the fix be pushed into a lean-active consumer repo, or left for those repos to pull on their own schedule?
options: Source-store only - fix and runtime-verify here, run check-consumer-freshness.sh read-only to name the stale lean-active consumers (~/Projects/BimodalLogic, ~/Projects/cslib, ~/Projects/Logos/Theory), and let each pull on its own schedule

Also deploy - run `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh ~/Projects/BimodalLogic` (the repo where the defect was observed) to regenerate its .claude/ tree and confirm the corrected strings landed there
user_decision.recommended: Source-store only - fix and runtime-verify here, run check-consumer-freshness.sh read-only to name the stale lean-active consumers (~/Projects/BimodalLogic, ~/Projects/cslib, ~/Projects/Logos/Theory), and let each pull on its own schedule

memory_candidates.content: In the agent-system source store (~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/**), a fix to an extension that is NOT in the source repo's own .claude-extensions.json cannot be deploy-verified in that repo: deploy-headless.sh force-loads core and resyncs only already-active extensions, so it regenerates no artifact for an inactive extension. Any acceptance criterion of the form 'deploy and confirm the regenerated .claude/** copies carry the fix' is therefore unsatisfiable in-repo for such an extension. The honest resolution is a read-only propagation record: confirm the touched files are deploy-carried by the extension's manifest.json provides.* blocks, then run check-consumer-freshness.sh --stale-only to name which registered consumer repos are behind. Pushing deploy-headless.sh into a consumer repo is technically possible (it takes a TARGET_REPO argument) but inverts the pull-only consumer architecture and drags every unrelated pending source change along, so it belongs behind an explicit user decision, not an implementer's default.
